text:
sara: FYI onboarding harbor-32b-int4 on dedicated testbed showed a reproducible drift after long priming (~16k tokens). attaching quick notes and a mini-repro.

sara: short repro: run resume_replay --model harbor-32b --quant int4 --anchor 16384 --resume sliding --seed 7 against longdoc(22k). observed token divergence ~16090-16110 window across runs.

omar: can you paste the minimal log lines around the divergence?

sara: sure: 
```
[2025-01-04 09:10:02] prefill: anchor_keys=16384
[2025-01-04 09:10:05] kv:write head0 pos=16088 key_hash=0x9bfa
[2025-01-04 09:10:05] gen:step token_idx=16095 kv_index=16095 got="and" expected=","
```

liam: interesting. is this specific to int4? how does fp16 behave?

sara: fp16 baseline - clean. int8 had very rare flips but int4 is consistent.

zhen: could be packing/unpacking of kv blocks for int4 causing subtle permutation of key order. we changed pack order in the int4 kernels to optimize alignment. did you try forcing slow path (unpacked) to compare?

sara: yep. forcing unpacked path removed the divergence. so kernel packing seems implicated.

omar: notes from earlier: harbor-32b uses rotary with per-head scaling (rotary_scale != 1.0) and we also apply a small position remapping for anchors > 8k in the compiler to avoid overflow. both could interact with packing.

liam: quick hypothesis: int4 packing reorder + position remap integer rounding -> different sin/cos index lookup -> head-wise phase drift -> small logit skew -> token flip.

bench-bot: @bench-bot run pack-order-sanity --model harbor-32b --quant int4 --anchors 8192,16384 --trials 6

bench-bot: Queued pack-order-sanity on runner-2. ETA 4m.

bench-bot: Partial results:
- anchor=8192: all trials aligned (no divergence)
- anchor=16384: 6/6 trials diverged in token window 16086..16112; flipped tokens differ but alignment rate ~97%.

zhen: thanks. two quick mitigation ideas: 1) revert pack-order change for anchors >= 8192 in the int4 kernels (simple but loses perf), 2) add deterministic index mapping in prefill that canonicalizes table indices before packing, 3) per-head phase correction like previous teams used.

omar: practical: we need canary-safe fix for Dedicated customers. option (2) sounds low-risk: canonicalize index math in prefill/runtime so packing order becomes irrelevant. can we implement a cheap patch?

sara: i prototyped a runtime shim that, before packing, permutes kv rows back into natural positions according to (pos % shard_size) ordering. flip gone in 50/50 quick trials. i can push PR with tests.

liam: performance tradeoff? doing a permute pre-pack costs memcpy cycles. how bad is it?

sara: microbench shows ~4% throughput hit on small batches, negligible on large batch sizes. for Dedicated canary we can accept 4% until we bounce to a kernel-level fix.

zhen: long-term we should update compiler to emit packed layout compatible with position remap, or change rotary index generation to be monotonic with packed layout. filing runtime+compiler tickets.

omar: test coverage: add a golden replay that runs the same seed across fp16/int8/int4 and asserts identical token sequence up to N=20k for the onboarding harness. sara, can you add that to your PR?

sara: yes. will add bench/test/gold_replay/harbor-32b-16k-seed7.json and a CI job that runs in serial to avoid nondet.

liam: also check KV checksum invariant we added last quarter: compute per-key checksum before and after packing; if delta > eps warn and optionally run canonicalizer. this could auto-detect future pack-induced drift.

bench-bot: Full run complete. Artifacts: /artifacts/pack_order_1715556789.tar.gz. Summary attached to ticket INF-4128.

omar: timeline: sara will open PR for the runtime shim today, enable it for int4 canary on dedicated for next week's run, and zhen will spec compiler change in follow-up.

sara: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eng-ml/pull/4890 - includes tests and perf notes.

liam: nice work. tagging @onboarding-pm and @dedicated-ops. please paste any extra traces to the ticket. :+1:

sara: one more datapoint: i ran a headwise-cos-sin diff between fp16 and int4-packed prefill tables and per-head phase offset averaged 0.002 radians on head 5-7, which correlates with earlier flips. i'll add the diff plots to the PR.

omar: cool. closing loop after canary. if anything else pops up ping here.
